items.title: Paul Smith interviewed by Monk Rowe, Los Angeles, California, February 14, 1999
items.q: [INTERVIEWER] Music from fellows like John Coltrane that are seemingly very serious and filled with let’s say messages, did that ever appeal to you? ... [INTERVIEWEE] No. I like melodic, good sounds.

ctx.x: I listen to Tatum, I listen to Oscar, I listen to Dick Hyman. Those are my three favorite pianists, as a pianist. I’ve got most of Peter Nero’s early stuff. He did what I always wanted to do and we couldn’t convince the people at CBS, I used to do all the Paul Weston dates and Paul wrote these beautiful string things. He was one of the better writers of that type of music. And we always wanted to do a piano thing with the string section and all that routine. And we couldn’t sell it to CBS and then RCA came out…
Music from fellows like John Coltrane that are seemingly very serious and filled with let’s say messages, did that ever appeal to you? © Fillius Jazz Archive -19-

No. I like melodic, good sounds. I like a guy that gets a good sound on his instrument. Like on alto sax I mean it’s hard to beat Paul Desmond with Brubeck. He got a lovely sound on the instrument. You could listen to him, he didn’t get that raucous sound. A lot of guys get a very raucous sound on their instrument, which is exciting if you’re playing raucous jazz, but the guys that I’ve always liked have gotten good sound.
